questions.q: For which type of bank account is manual reconciliation ideally suited as a primary approach?
options: Accounts with a high volume of monthly transactions
Accounts with a small volume of monthly transactions
Only payroll accounts
Accounts that have never had a bank statement loaded
questions.explain: Manual reconciliation is ideally suited to accounts with a small volume of monthly transactions, where matching rules aren't worth maintaining.

questions.q: Why does even a high-volume account, mostly handled by automatic reconciliation, still rely on manual reconciliation?
options: It doesn't — high-volume accounts never need manual reconciliation
To handle the exceptions automatic reconciliation couldn't confidently match
Because automatic reconciliation is always disabled on high-volume accounts
Because manual reconciliation runs before automatic reconciliation
questions.explain: Manual reconciliation is where exceptions left behind by automatic reconciliation get resolved, regardless of the account's overall volume.

questions.q: What is distinct about a tolerance rule used during manual reconciliation, compared to one used in an automatic matching rule?
options: It can be assigned directly to the bank account, separate from a matching rule's tolerance
It is identical in every way and cannot be configured separately
It only applies to Many to Many match types
It can never allow any variance at all
questions.explain: A tolerance rule can be assigned directly to a bank account for use during manual reconciliation, independent of the tolerance tied to an automatic matching rule.

questions.q: What can a Cash Manager do during manual reconciliation when a statement line has no existing system counterpart, such as a bank fee?
options: Nothing — the line must remain unreconciled forever
Delete the statement line from the file
Create the missing external transaction directly during reconciliation
Automatically reverse the bank statement
questions.explain: A Cash Manager can create the missing external transaction on the fly during manual reconciliation rather than leaving the line stuck.

questions.q: In the worked example, what judgment did the Cash Manager apply to the $4,998.00 statement line against a $5,000.00 receipt?
options: Rejected the match entirely and requested a refund
Confirmed it was the same payment, short by a $2.00 bank-deducted wire fee
Automatically let a one-to-one matching rule resolve it
Reversed the original Receivables receipt
questions.explain: The Cash Manager used judgment, supported by remittance advice, to confirm the $2.00 difference was a bank-deducted wire fee rather than a mismatch.
